payload.title: Nsight Profiling in Practice
payload.summary: > Compiled from multiple technical articles in the Zhihu community, covering practical topics including Nsight Systems system-level analysis, Nsight Compute kernel-level analysis, Warp Stall diagnosis, and Roofline analysis.

sections.heading: 1. Tool Overview: Nsight Systems vs Nsight Compute
sections.gist: NVIDIA provides two layers of performance analysis tools, targeting performance bottlenecks at different granularities:

sections.heading: 2. Nsight Systems in Practice
sections.gist: Key parameter descriptions: - `--trace`: Specifies the types of APIs to trace; `cuda` traces CUDA runtime/driver API, `nvtx` traces user markers - `--delay` / `--duration`: Controls the collection time window to avoid capturing irrelevant …

sections.heading: 3. Nsight Compute in Practice
sections.gist: `--set detailed` collects complete performance metrics, including all panels such as Roofline, Occupancy, Memory, Compute, and Scheduler.

sections.heading: 4. Warp Stall Cause Analysis
sections.gist: When a warp is not in the Eligible state, it is in the Stall state.

sections.heading: 5. Practical Tips and Common Pitfalls
sections.gist: **Misconception 1**: GPU utilization at 100% = performance is already optimal

sections.heading: 6. eGPU: Next-Generation GPU Performance Analysis Framework
sections.gist: eGPU is an observability framework that offloads eBPF bytecode to the GPU through dynamic PTX injection, representing a new direction in GPU performance analysis:

implementation.snippet:
```bash
# profiling
nsys profile -o output_report ./my_app

# recommendedparameter
nsys profile \
 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \ # CUDA API, NVTX , OS row
 --duration=30 \ # 30 seconds
 --delay=5 \ # 5 seconds
 --cudabacktrace=true \ # CUDA
    --output=report \
    ./my_app

# PyTorch
nsys profile \
    --trace=cuda,nvtx,cudnn,cublas \
    -o training_report \
    python train.py
```

```python
# PyTorch use NVTX
import torch

with torch.cuda.nvtx.range("forward_pass"):
    output = model(input)

with torch.cuda.nvtx.range("backward_pass"):
    loss.backward()

with torch.cuda.nvtx.range("optimizer_step"):
    optimizer.step()
```

```cpp
// CUDA C++ use NVTX
#include <nvtx3/nvToolsExt.h>

nvtxRangePush("matrix_multiply");
kernel<<<grid, block>>>(args);
nvtxRangePop();
```

```bash
# analysis( kernel)
ncu --set detailed -o report ./my_app

# analysis kernel
ncu --set detailed --kernel-name "regex:gemm" -o report ./my_app

# recommendedcompilation(keep)
nvcc -O3 -lineinfo -arch=sm_90 kernel.cu -o kernel
```

```
│
├── Selected (execute)

```
